key_insight: Variational quantum classifiers showed a trade-off between circuit expressivity and training stability, but classical models outperformed them on synthetic network traffic.
engineering_relevance: VQC architecture and optimizer choices materially affect anomaly detection, with no demonstrated advantage over classical baselines in this study.
method: Generate synthetic network traffic for anomaly detection.
Evaluate four VQC architectures varying feature encoding, ansatz, quantum neural network type, and optimizer.
Compare classification performance against Support Vector Machine and Random Forest models.
evidence_signal: VQC-4 reached up to 89.0% accuracy, VQC-3 was identified as best overall using ZFeatureMap, RealAmplitudes, and ADAM, and classical baselines achieved perfect classification on the synthetic data.
watch_item: Synthetic data with relatively simple class separations limits real-world conclusions; deeper VQCs were training-sensitive, and VQC-2 produced many false negatives.
paper_title: Quantum Anomaly Detection in network traffic using Variational Quantum Classifiers
